Article 26 of the ICSID Convention states as follows:“Consent of the parties to arbitration under this Convention shall, unless otherwise stated, be deemed consent to such arbitration to the exclusion of any other remedy. A Contracting State may require the exhaustion of local administrative or judicial remedies as a condition of its consent to arbitration under this Convention.”-an application of the court’s wide inherent powers to manage proceedings before the court-test to stay proceedings pending another court’s proceeding, pending an appeal from that court or pending other arbitral proceedings-Special circumstances-prevent injustice and abuse of court process-the determination of stay applications requires an exercise of balancing many of the ingredients enshrined in the overriding objective: the avoidance of excessive cost, the unnecessary expenditure of finite public resources, the right of every litigant to expeditious justice, the minimising of litigation delays, managing the interface and overlap between two judicial organisations, the allocation of limited judicial resources and, broadly, the convenience of all concerned. judgments.title: Akamai Technologies International AG v Ketua Pengarah Hasil Dalam Negeri & ors
judgments.catchwords: Revenue Law — Income Tax — Withholding Tax — Payments by a Malaysian subsidiary to its Swiss parent under a Services Reseller Agreement for the right to market, resell and support the parent's internet content delivery and cloud services — Whether such Services Reseller Payments constitute "royalties" chargeable to withholding tax under s 109 of the Income Tax Act 1967 — Whether, by virtue of s 132 ITA, the definition of "royalty" in Article 12 of the Malaysia–Switzerland Double Taxation Agreement ("MSDTA") must prevail over the definition in s 2 ITA — Whether a narrower domestic classification could displace the treaty — Whether remuneration for services involving the provider's own skill, technology and proprietary systems, without any impartation of special commercial knowledge or transfer, grant or use of know-how or proprietary rights, is royalty — Judicial Review — Availability of judicial review notwithstanding an alternative statutory appeal to the Special Commissioners under ss 99 and 109H ITA — Whether filing of Form Q barred review — Whether the existence of an alternative remedy precluded review where the complaint was clear illegality, excess of jurisdiction, blatant failure to perform statutory duty or breach of the rules of natural justice — Whether disputes raising discrete questions of law (statutory construction and interpretation of a written agreement) were suitable for judicial review — Additional Assessments — Whether assessments for earlier years of assessment were time-barred under sub-s 91(3) ITA in the absence of any allegation, consideration or satisfaction of the statutory preconditions of fraud, wilful default or negligence — Natural Justice — Whether the Revenue's failure to give reasons for departing from binding decisions, for issuing time-barred assessments and for imposing a 45% penalty breached the common law duty of fairness — Certiorari, declaration, mandamus and prohibition — Whether exceptional circumstances warranted intervention — Held: applications allowed; the Revenue erred in law by applying s 2 ITA without giving effect to Article 12 MSDTA contrary to s 132 ITA; the Services Reseller Payments were not royalties; the assessments for the time-barred years were issued without satisfying sub-s 91(3) ITA; and the failure to give adequate reasons was procedurally unfair.
